1.why: Every authenticated endpoint derives the account exclusively from the server-side session (session.accountId); no client-supplied user identifier is ever accepted, so MFA settings are bound to the signed-in owner with no IDOR path.

2.why: The identity code (123456) and authenticator code (654321) are hardcoded global constants rather than per-user values, so the same code would validate for any account in the system.

3.why: Enabling MFA in /api/authenticator/verify only mutates account fields and never deletes or rotates entries in the sessions map, so previously issued sessions continue to work.

4.why: The TOTP secret is stored AES-256-GCM encrypted via crypt() and recovery codes are stored as salted PBKDF2-SHA-256 hashes with 210,000 iterations, never in plain text at rest.

5.why: The OTP secret, both verification codes, and all eight recovery codes are hardcoded deterministic constants, not generated by a CSPRNG; crypto.getRandomValues is only used for session/CSRF tokens, salts, and IVs.

6.why: The only cookie set is mfa_session with HttpOnly, Secure and SameSite=Strict and no secret is placed in any cookie, though the CSRF token and mock secrets are delivered in JSON bodies and client-side storage code is not visible.

7.why: Server-side validation is enforced via field() length/type checks, an email regex, a strict 6-digit OTP regex, a recovery-code charset regex and JSON-only size-limited bodies, with in-memory maps eliminating SQL injection, though no phone input exists.

8.why: Responses are JSON-encoded, the otpauth label is passed through encodeURIComponent, and a strict nonce-based CSP with default-src 'self' is set, but the truncated frontend rendering code cannot be inspected for DOM encoding.

9.why: No redirect logic or Location headers appear anywhere in the visible code, so neither an open redirect nor an allow-list of internal destinations can be confirmed.

10.why: Every response sets CSP, Strict-Transport-Security, X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, X-Frame-Options: DENY and frame-ancestors 'none', plus Referrer-Policy and Permissions-Policy.

11.why: The cookie() builder emits mfa_session with HttpOnly, Secure and SameSite=Strict attributes (plus Path and Max-Age), and expiredCookie() mirrors them on clearing.

12.why: No logging exists, error messages are generic with no stack traces, but the OTP seed appears in the otpauth URI query string and mock codes/documentation strings are returned in routine API responses.

13.why: Identity codes via check() are single-use and expire after 15 minutes, but the authenticator verify path never checks used or expires before accepting and the mock documentation explicitly states the code 'does not expire in this mock.'

14.why: Failed attempts increment counters that trigger a 10-minute lockout after 5 failures across identity verify, authenticator verify, and password sign-in, with recovery attempt/lockout fields also tracked.

15.why: A fresh CSPRNG session ID is issued at sign-in with enforced 30-minute idle and 8-hour absolute timeouts, but the logout handler lies in the truncated portion of the file with only the expiredCookie() helper visible.
